characters.name: In General
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: At a school that is mostly for wealthy students, low-class students are bullied by eithercondescending it girlslike Lu orarrogant classist jerkslike Guzmán, the staff present either doesn't give a damn about their wellbeingor simply give them a short suspension. Lu was suspended for two months for bribing a teacher into giving her the top score while Guzmán was suspended for three days, both ahead of the final exams, when Lu lied that he was the one who started a fight with Samuel over Polo. However, some exceptions could include Azucena (the former principal), Jessica (the P.E. teacher) and Luis (the head of studies), and two teachers who broke up Samuel and Guzmán's fight after Lu blew the whistle on them. Alpha Bitch:This show has no shortage of mean girl characters across its seasons:Lucrecia (Season 1): The original queen bee—intelligent, stylish, and viciously sharp-tongued. She rules Las Encinas with icy confidence and isn’t afraid to put others in their place.Ari (Season 4): Takes over as the new power girl—cold, composed, and manipulative, with a strong sense of superiority and a no-nonsense attitude.Sara & Isadora (Later Seasons): Both carry the Alpha Bitch mantle in their own ways—Sara through influence and social media manipulation, and Isadora through her wealth, club girl status, and emotional detachment.Emilia (Season 8): Keeps the tradition alive—ambitious, calculating, and ruthless, maintaining her dominance through charm and intimidation. Lucrecia (Season 1): The original queen bee—intelligent, stylish, and viciously sharp-tongued. She rules Las Encinas with icy confidence and isn’t afraid to put others in their place. Ari (Season 4): Takes over as the new power girl—cold, composed, and manipulative, with a strong sense of superiority and a no-nonsense attitude. Sara & Isadora (Later Seasons): Both carry the Alpha Bitch mantle in their own ways—Sara through influence and social media manipulation, and Isadora through her wealth,

characters.name: Iván Carvalho
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: He never actually says he's attracted to men and women, but still hooks up with Patrick, Ari and made out with Isadora. When Patricks questions in season 6 if he's in love with his sister, he just answers that he's not in love with anyone. Also Iván had started a relationship with Puleng from “Blood and Water”. Beware the Nice Ones: He’s normally a nice guy, but these are the times that he will get angry if anyone dares to threaten him or disrespect him. Break the Cutie: The death of his father Cruz ends up crumbling his world to pieces, shedding the cheerful, funny and optimistic person he used to be, now twistingto a depressed, resentful and indifferent one.In season 8, He was very distressed when the cops framed him for Joel’s murder. In season 8, He was very distressed when the cops framed him for Joel’s murder. Calling the Old Man Out: Usually prone to calling his father out for his immature behaviour.

characters.name: Isadora Artiñán
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: She seems to be drawn to Phillipe, who pursues her for love him and keeps supporting for him being a rapist. Attention Whore: Isadora is accused of this by almost everyone (sans for Ari, Mencía, Rocío and Nico), including Dídac initially, at the school due to the lack of proof about the boys' participation in her rape. Break the Haughty: After wasting her energies defending a rapist like Phillipe, Isadora herself getsrapedby three guys she hung out with at an Ibiza party she hosted.In season 8, Her family goes broke, her party that the decorations that Omar told her not to nearly killed everyone, Her father was murdered in prison and this is what leads Roberta disowning her. This poor girl needs a hug. In season 8, Her family goes broke, her party that the decorations that Omar told her not to nearly killed everyone, Her father was murdered in prison and this is what leads Roberta disowning her. This poor girl needs a hug. Dating What Daddy Hates: Her reasoning of not wanting to be with Didac because of her family and Didac’s family feud.

characters.name: Sara
characters.description: Aesop Amnesia: Sara learned in season 7 to stop bending to an abusive guy like Raúl, all thanks to her self-defense teacher Jessica. However, in season 8, she has failed to make any progress whatsoever, as Sara obsesses over avenging Raúl after finding out about his death. Ambiguously Bi: She has Raul as her boyfriend, but she seems to be attracted to Mencia. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Her abusive relationship with Raúl. Despite being aware of his nature, Sara is afraid to leave him and often brushes off any genuine concern people might show about it. Berserk Button: Her button is pushed by the people (namely Mencia and Jessica) who see through Raul's abusive nature and encourage her to leave him. But when Isadora at one point also becomes concerned upon learning that Raul proposed to her,Sara stays calm and simply diverts the subject by asking Isadora how her relationship with Didac is doing. Blaming the Victim: Sara does this fully to Chloe after she recorded Chloe doing the nasty with Raul and then blaming her for Raul’s death.

characters.name: Nico
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: When confronting Ari for her transphobic behavior and rejecting him over Bilal with this direct question:"What does Bilal have that I don't?" "What does Bilal have that I don't?" Be Careful What You Wish For: Nico shows open resentment to Eric and Chloe's relationship and is always wishing for Chloe to leave him. This wishdoescome true, courtesy of Emilia, who switched Eric's medications with drugs to manipulate Chloe into doubting her boyfriend's word, and later when her and Carmen are forced to move out of the city when Sara finds out about their role in Raúl's death. Betty and Veronica: He is the Betty to Bilal's Veronica for Ari's Archie. Beware the Nice Ones: For instance, when it comes to Ari, Nico literally called her out by her transphobia.

characters.name: Sonia
characters.description: A Friend in Need: With Omar. Betty and Veronica: The Betty to Ari's Veronica for Nico the Archie. Beware the Nice Ones: Sonia always speaks her truth, even in the first episode of season eight, she called police out whenever he’s making a racist injustice, comments and assumptions about her boyfriend, Dalmar. Butt-Monkey: Sonia may be the sanest out of all characters, but this poor girl gets cheated on by both of her boyfriends with someone beautiful like Ari and later Chloe. Double Standard: Sonia had no issue whatsoever trying to make a friendship with Ari and see if she needed any help, but with Chloe she refused to do that because of her infamous sexual reputation at the school, as well as catching her and Nico having sex and feeling jealous about it. At one point, while helping Omar out with the self-help app, she tells him she's doubting what he told her that people deserve to be helped, whether they're good or bad.

characters.name: Joel
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: Joel grows into this by season 8, blackmailing Carmen and Chloe by threatening to tell the police about Raúl's murder unless they helped Dalmar not to be deported to his country and even bravely threatening Luis for stalking Isadora. Bury Your Gays: A final queer character to be murdered of the series. Dark and Troubled Past: He was kicked out by his parents after he came out as gay and had to live on the streets. Dude Magnet: Omar and Iván are attracted to Joel, and he returns this to each of them. Héctor, the Alumni president, also has eyes for him. Horrible Judge of Character: Las Encinas when it comes to Joel, as he wishes to achieve things there including the Alumni club and completely ignores Omar advising him against studying there, due to its infamous reputation regarding the murders and covered-up incidents. This sadly results in Joel being murdered.Downplayedwith Raúl, as Joel was unaware that he was an abusive boyfriend to Sara.

characters.name: Chloe
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Like Sara, she also ended up getting romantically involved with Raúl and for once almost having to endure his abusive outbursts.Downplayedwith Eric, who has anger issues but tries to work on himself and is genuinely interested in making a connection with Chloe. Attention Whore: And how. Her infamous reputation of having sexual encounter with guys and record them on video makes her this to the eyes of the student body.The ''so-called'' story about her sex video being leaked as her cellphone was stolen is clearly a lie. Berserk Button: Using Chloe's habit ofgetting aroundto one's advantage will definitely get on her nerves. Betty and Veronica: She is the self-centered Veronica to Sonia's caring and comprehensive Betty for Nico. Break the Haughty: After her video with Raúl is posted, Chloe's image is further shattered by Sara when she makes her as guilty as he was, and Sara painting herself as a "victim".

characters.name: Eric
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: When Nico gets angry at Eric for allowing Rocío to be arrested, he straightforwardly asks him what was he doing when that happened. In response, Nico stays silent, knowing it was because he was having sex with Chloe. Betty and Veronica: He's a broken guy in need of help, which makes him a Veronica, while Raúl is a wealthy and devilishly handsome influencer who has the position of a Betty. However, when it comes to character, Eric's efforts in making an emotional connection with Chloe make him a Betty, and Raúl's history of sexism and masculine toxicity result in him becoming the Veronica. Chick Magnet: Chloe and Rocío were both attracted to him. Cool Big Bro: Actuallycousin, but this is one the few reasons why Nico begs his parents, mostly his father, to give him a chance despite his mental health issues, because he looks up to him. Did Not Get the Girl: Chloe leaves Madrid due to her and her mother trying to escape from the police for Raúl's murder.

characters.name: Malick
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He appears to be loyal and charming at first, but he later cheats on Nadia with Omar and reveals his careless nature. Gayngst: Malick hides his homosexuality from Nadia's family in order to meet their expectations of him. The Hedonist: He is well-mannered, but tends to party a lot and drink gin tonics. Nice Guy: Despite being rich like the other students, this is his most defining trait. Put on a Bus: Graduates from Las Encinas and leaves for New York with Lu and Nadia.

characters.name: Yeray
characters.description: Because You Were Nice to Me: Yeray’s crush on Carla stems from her staunchly defending him on an Instagram post when he was being cyberbullied. In the Season Three finale, he also buys her family’s wineries and signs control cove to her after she points out that he has nothing to prove to any of his old bullies and they break up. Devoted to You: Yeray has been in love with Carla for years because shemade a comment defending himwhen he was being cyber-bullied over his weight,to the point that even saves her family’s winery business. Formerly Fat: He used to be overweight which made him a target for bullies. He likes Carla because she was the only one to stand up for him when he was fat. Nice Guy: He's shown to to be nice and polite. He and Carla break up in a friendly way. Put on a Bus: He makes his last appearance in the seventh episode of the third season, so it's implied that he had graduated from Las Encinas.

characters.name: Patrick Blanco Commerford
characters.description: Age-Gap Romance: With Cruz, in season 5. Big Brother Instinct: He was worried that Mencia would commit suicide all because of her mother's death to the point if he doesn't come home to his family for christmas. Composite Character: He's a mix of Polo and Valerio (the later being himself reminescent of Christian): he's rich, loves parties, uses drugs and had a complicated polyamorous relationship. Dude Magnet: Ander, Omar and Ivan. Easily Forgiven: Despite the tension Patrick caused by damaging Ander and Omar’s relationship, by Season 5, Patrick and Omar appear to be on amicable terms after they sleep together.

characters.name: Ariadna "Ari" Blanco Commerford
characters.description: Academic Alpha Bitch: And how, right down to the decorations in her locker. The Alcoholic: One of her defining traits in Season 6. Alpha Bitch: After Lu’s departure at the end of season 3, Ari steps in as the new role in season 4 of Elite. As the wealthy and entitled daughter of the new principal, she quickly asserts dominance at Las Encinas. Ari is snooty, manipulative, and often condescending toward the existing main cast. Ambiguously Evil: Season 6 ends with Ari getting Mencía, whom she believes (and Mencía herself as well) to be responsible for Iván's accident, out of trouble using their father's connections. But it's unclear if she still trusts him after he killed Samuel, while Patrick and Mencía keep their distance from him. Berserk Button: More often than not in Season 6.After Samuel dies, she is always annoyed at the mention of his name, especially when she hasn't even had the courage to visit his grave and properly mourn him for months, something her siblings call her out on. This is clearly a coping mechanism, when she rejects Bilal, Nico and even Ivan of all people.She has the tendency to drink a lot of alcohol, causing her siblings, friends and even Sonia to be worried about this and try their best to help her out. However, Ari, regularly in a fit of rage, rejects any of this by telling them that she'sfine,even though she isn't.

characters.name: Mencía Blanco Commerford
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: When Ari and Mencía fight over Benjamín's trial where he may be declared innocent of Samuel's death, with Mencía outright refusing to testify on his behalf, Ari tries to convince her by pointing out that everything he has done for them was for their own good. Mencía strikes back by asking if him killing Samuel was worth the effort. Betty and Veronica:In Season 5, with Mencia unable to be in a relationship with Rebeka, she moves on by dating another girl named Jess, which makes Mencia jealous. Due to Jess' personality, she is the Veronica to Mencia's Betty.In Season 6, while Sara is in an abusive relationship with Raul, she serves as the Betty to Raul's Veronica. In Season 5, with Mencia unable to be in a relationship with Rebeka, she moves on by dating another girl named Jess, which makes Mencia jealous. Due to Jess' personality, she is the Veronica to Mencia's Betty. In Season 6, while Sara is in an abusive relationship with Raul, she serves as the Betty to Raul's Veronica. Black Sheep: She has conflicts with her family especially with her father because she was blamed for her mother's death. This is ultimately subverted when they found out about her sexual relationship with Armando.

characters.name: Phillipe Von Triesenberg
characters.description: The Atoner: At the end of the series after being confronted by Cayetana, he leaves a voicemail message to an unknown woman. She is a previous victim of his. Phillip looks to atone by apologising by voicemail and confirming that he did the act so that she could go to the authorities or media. Bilingual Bonus: Speaks French on a few occasions with Benjamin and with his mother. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: You think he’s some kind of charming and harmless royal prince to be around with, but once Cayetana watched the recorded video of them making love and then in the early season 5 of him revealing to be a rapist of Elodie and sexually assaulting other girls. He’s clearly not a good role model. Broken Pedestal: Cayetana was devastated to learn that Phillipe was involved with Elodie and later on when he tries to rape her at his car. Chick Magnet: Due to his royal status, he attracted a lot of girls, including his ex Elodie, Cayetana and Isadora.

characters.name: Hugo Múler
characters.description: Arc Villain: From season 5 to 6, Hugo is the antagonist to Isadora's character arc of being a victim of sexual assault. Big Bad: Becomes this in season 6 when he and his two other friends seek by all means to get away with what they did to Isadora back in Ibiza. Becomes aBig Bad Ensemblewith Raúl, who is abusive to Sara in their relationship. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He pretends to be friendly with Isadora when he, his two friends and Ivan join her on a trip to Ibiza where they party a lot. However, he shows his true face once Isadora gets heavily drunk and takes advantage of this. Blatant Lies: When he, Alex, Javier and Isadora are summoned by Virginia about their fight at the halls over the rape allegations, Hugo smugly tells her that his friends were "assaulted". However, this isn't entirely true, as all Ari and Mencia did was drug them and write the word "RAPIST" on their backs. Hate Sink: Possibly the most despicable character in the show's run. Is shown at various times being homophobic, transphobic, highly sexist and racist as well as being a rapist.

characters.name: Javier
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Response: When Dídac asks Javier if he would stay by his side even after finding out he was a rapist, Javier answers that at least he would be willing to hear his side of the story and find a way to forgive him. Only for Dídac to tell him that it's up to Isadora whether or not to forgive him. The Atoner: After a lot of doubts, he ultimately reports the assault on Isadora as a way to make it up for her and Dídac. Conflicting Loyalty: He chooses to support Isadora over sticking with Hugo and Alex. Expy: To Polo, as he was best friends with Dídac until he refused to talk to him after finding out about his involvement in Isadora's rape, becoming clearly remorseful for it. Unlike Polo, though, he lived to face justice for the crime. Heel–Face Turn: Starts feeling remorseful for assisting Hugo and Alex in raping Isadora and for straining his long-term friendship with Dídac.

characters.name: Alejandro Díaz
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Like Hugo, he also puts on a friendly mask to Isadora before raping her at the Ibiza party. Blatant Lies: When Nico reacts angrily to Alex staring at his junk, he claims that he's just curious about how to pee without a penis. Nico doesn't believe him at all and calls him stupid. Karma Houdini Warranty: Alex ets arrested alongside Hugo and Javier, the latter of whom tipped off the police out of remorse. Put on a Prison Bus: He gets arrested for raping Isadora, alongside Hugo and Javier.

characters.name: Dídac
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: When Javier tries to defend himself to Dídac while confronted for raping Isadora saying that friendsa always stick together even if they mess up real bad and that he would never abandon him, Dídac strikes back with this question:"Even if I was a rapist?"To which Javier quickly answers: "At least I'd hear your side of the story, then I would find a way to forgive you". "Even if I was a rapist?" To which Javier quickly answers: "At least I'd hear your side of the story, then I would find a way to forgive you". Conflicting Loyalty: He is in love with Isadora and sides with her instead of his friend Javier, who was an accomplice in her rape, and his family who is feuded with Isadora's over business drama. Contrasting Sequel Main Character: To Guzmán. Both are rich students from Las Encinas with childhood best friends of their own that have commited a crime, but Guzmán is initially mean to some of the characters and prone to outbursts and violence while Dídac is a good-hearted person who is able to maintain his composure.

characters.name: Rocío
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Rocío starts falling in love with the rebellious self-destructive Eric in season 7. Ascended Extra: She gets more prominence in season 7 with the introduction of her mother, a corrupt judge bribed by Isadora's father, with whom she has a strained relationship. Betty and Veronica:Downplayedwith Rocio the Betty and Ari the Veronica for Bilal in season 6.In season 7, she is the Betty to Chloe's Veronica for Eric (Archie). Downplayedwith Rocio the Betty and Ari the Veronica for Bilal in season 6. In season 7, she is the Betty to Chloe's Veronica for Eric (Archie).

characters.name: Emilia Krawietz
characters.description: Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Emilia is dark-haired, she is rude, snooty and a blunt woman. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Emilia appears as a cordial and helpful person who wants people to be in alumni club to have best interest in mind. But she is revealed to be a horrid, nasty and an elitist person. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: She's very classist, racist, Muslimphobic to Omar and looks down on the low-class students like Lu, except that Lu had some redeeming qualities (such as her relationship with Guzmán, caring for her half-brother Valerio, and becoming good friends with Omar in season 2, and later Nadia in season 3) and became a nice person, while Emilia has ZERO redeeming qualities and cares about no one but herself. Disc-One Final Boss: Her and Héctor were the most active antagonists in season 8 until their arrest and early release. Luis takes over as the true main antagonist and the culprit behind Joel's murder. Dislikes the New Guy: She looks down on Joel as the moment when Hector invited him in the alumni place.

characters.name: Héctor Krawietz
characters.description: Affably Evil: He’s a massive prick who blackmails Joel, but he became quite friendly to him for a while, very tolerable and lets him stay at the alumni place. Alas, Poor Villain: His grief over Joel's death is quite pitiable and heartbreaking. Blackmail: Virginia is stopped by Hector wanting to expel Joel for recording the girls showering threatening to sue her and the school for malpractice. He also blackmails Omar into staying quiet about his assault planning to have Nadia's internship at the UN revoked. Break the Haughty: Despite Hector being a great asshole for attacking Omar, his sadness over Joel's death is quite genuine and pitiable. Disc-One Final Boss: He and Emilia were the most active antagonists in season 8 until their arrest and early release. Luis takes over as the true main antagonist and the culprit behind Joel's murder.

characters.name: Pier and Guillermina
characters.description: Foreign Exchange Student: Pier is Italian and attended Las Encinas as an exchange student. Happily Married: they have been married for several years and they love each other. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Despite her high status, Guillermina is shown to be a nice woman and even takes a quick liking to Joel, compared to the classist Emilia. Mrs. Robinson: Guillermina seduces Joel alongside her husband Pier.

characters.name: Bilal
characters.description: Apologises a Lot: Bilal for unceremoniously arriving at Samuel and Omar's house, with Samuel clearly not liking him, then his visit causing both of them to fight and eventually Samuel kicks Omar out of his house. Bilal does this once more when he brings Samuel, against Omar's wishes (as he had told him to bring Rebeka to deal with Armando's corpse), in an attempt to intervene and mend their conflict. Chick Magnet: He caught the attention of Rocio and Ari. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He disappears without a trace after the events of season 6. Everyone Has Standards: He is completely uncomfortable with Hugo, Alex and Javier showing up at Isadora's club after they raped her in Ibiza. Despite his best efforts, though, they refuse to leave. Gold Digger: It's heavily implied part of the reason he starts showing interest in Rocio is because she buys him expensive gifts.

characters.name: Raúl
characters.description: Armor-Piercing Question: He asks Sara one about himself: "Sara, do you think I'm a monster?" Asshole Victim: He is pushed off the balcony by Carmen and dies instantly. Taking into account how abusive Raúl was to Sara, and later Chloewho was going to repeat the same cycle, and him attempting to choke Carmen, who angrily points out he doesn't know how to respect women, no one will miss him at all. Well, no one except Sara. The Bad Guy Wins: Raul successfully gets back with Sara after he drugs Mencia, and Sara calls him to let him know that she accidentally injured Ivan. He decides to cover up his girlfriend's involvement and put the blame on Mencia.Subvertedin season 7, when Carmen has Raúl done for by pushing him off a balcony to his death. However, once again played straight in season 8 when Sara becomes obsessed with avenging Raúl. Once she finds out Carmen killed him, Sara tells Eric to tell Chloe she's going to report both her and Carmen to the police. Even in death, Raúl is still able to control Sara. Batman Gambit: He records a live streaming for his fans, promising to be a better boyfriend for Sara in order to get her to take him back. Predictably enough, she does. Be Careful What You Wish For: Raúl tells Sara that he'd rather kill himself than allowing her to report her role in Iván's hit-and-run to the police while guilt-tripping her into staying quiet. At the end of season 7, Carmen kills Raúl by pushing him off a balcony and lies to the police that he hadkilledhimself.

characters.name: Dalmar
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Dalmar gets more focus in season 8 once he's revealed to have the video of Carmen murdering Raúl. The Comically Serious: In most of his interactions with Joel and Omar he is a bit grouchy, but still a nice person deep down. Joel also lampshades this in season 8 when he offers Dalmar to move in with him and Iván. Chekhov's Gunman: The last episode of season 7 surprisingly reveals Dalmar as the only witness of Raúl's murder caused by Carmen, as he was coincidentally making a delivery around the same block. He even recorded the whole thing on his phone with Carmen on the roof. Let's see what he'll do with this newfound evidence in the upcoming final season. Good Counterpart: To Nano. Both resort to blackmail a person for money to achieve a goal out of desperation. Nano is a violent ex-convict who goes after Marina and Carla's families to settle pending debts he owes to some thugs who protected him in jail, while Dalmar is a kind-hearted guy who attempts to use Carmen's murder of Raúl against her in order to not be deported to his country when his status as an illegal inmigrant becomes threatened. Hero with Bad Publicity: Goes through this when the Alumni siblings frame him for Joel's murder.

characters.name: Nano García Domínguez
characters.description: Adaptation Name Change: InClass, he is Neeraj Kumar Valmiki. Big Bad Ensemble: With Carla for the first season. While she goes to greath lengths to both protect Polo and her family's reputations by retrieving her father's red watch containing sensitive information regarding his and Marina's father shady business, Nano, on the other hand, blackmails their families into paying the money he is demanding to settle bigger debts he owes to some thugs who protected him in jail. Big Brother Instinct: He genuinely cares about and is fiercly protective of Samuel, having a warm relationship with him - albeit not without its rough patches. Like with Guzman, it sometimes veers intoKnight Templar Big Brotherterritory, which is something he's completely unrepentant about, no matter how much trouble it causes for Samuel."I don't blame him. If I thought he (Guzman) killed my brother,I'd do the same." "I don't blame him. If I thought he (Guzman) killed my brother,I'd do the same." Break the Haughty: Not only does Nano's blackmail plot cause his relationship with Samuel to suffer, but it leads to Marina's death and his arrest due to being falsely accused of being her killer.

characters.name: Pilar
characters.description: Mama Bear: She has her moments, particularly towards Samuel. When the thugs Nano is in debt to ransack their house, she furiously chews him out for potentially getting Samuel hurt or killed... not that it stops her from leaving him to move to Morocco. Outliving One's Offspring:Her son Samuel is killed in season 5, and we never get so see her reaction to the news. Parents as People: Loves her sons, but clearly struggles with the responsibilities of raising them on her own, especially considering that Nano can't stay out of trouble. Put on a Bus: Leaves the show at the start of Season 3 to go be with Nano in Morocco. Shipper on Deck: She's very friendly to Marina and supportive of her relationship with Samuel.

characters.name: Yusef Shanaa
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: He makes a small cameo in season 7 with Imán when Omar is about to move in with his parents. Character Development: Originally portrayed as a stern, occasionally volatile father and a devout Muslim who believes his children are being corrupted by Spanish values and losing their own, Yusef eventually grows to accept Nadia's choices and Omar's sexuality and has a better relationship with his children for it. Hero Antagonist: For the entire subplot when it came to Omar, whose sexual orientantion he originally rejected, and being overly controlling to both him and Nadia. Not to mention his dislike for Guzmán. Horrible Judge of Character: He thinks both Guzman and the school she attends are a bad influence to Nadia, to the point he even threatens to take her out. Turns out before in Omar’s case, he was right. Immigrant Parents: From Palestine, whereas almost everybody in the show think they´re from Morocco.Truth in Televisionas Spain has a large Moroccan immigrant population but far fewer Palestinian migrants.

characters.name: Imán
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: She makes a small cameo in season 7 with Yusef when Omar is about to move in with his parents. Comically Missing the Point: Nadia wakes up from herErotic Dreamabout Guzmán, but her mom thinks she was screaming. Nadia plays along with her misinterpretation, claiming she was having a "nightmare". Open-Minded Parent: Unlike her husband Yusef, she seems to be sort of supportive of Omar's sexual orientation. Morality Pet: To Yusef. Parental Substitute: She acts like this to Lu when she reveals that her parents disowned her, telling her she'll always have a family with the Shanaas.

characters.name: Teodoro Rosón
characters.description: Affably Evil: He is very calm and cordial in behavior despite how dangerous he is, although in the first season the only time he ever loses his temper is when Nano blackmailed him with his stolen red watch and complained about the situtation to Carla. Abusive Parents: Carla's parents are shown in season 3 to be absolute nightmares, especially her father. He firstly threatens to harm Samuel, whom he knows Carla loves, so that way she will comply with what he wants and not risk his shady business dealings being exposed. Then he essentially prostitutes her to her wealthy classmate Jeray, having her basically act as an accesory rather than an equal partner with her own mind, to save the family's bankrupt wineries. It is revealed in a later episode that her mother knew the entire time and agreed to this, encouraging Carla to maintain the relationship Corrupt Corporate Executive: He and Ventura, his business partner and Guzman and Marina's father, are responsible for the collapse of the San Esteban school and cover their tracks by arranging to have Samuel, Nadia and Christian attend the elitist Las Encinas insitution, where their children also study. Greater-Scope Villain: He is the overarching antagonist in the first three seasons since he holds more threat than Carla, theBig Bad, and the reason why she needs to get the watch back from Marina that resulted in her murder by Polo in the first place to prevent his secrets and crimes held in said watch from being exposed to the world. Karma Houdini: Although Polo was posthumously declared guilty of Marina's murder in the end (thus absolving Nano of all culpability), he still got away with hiding both his complicity in the crime and all of the previous deeds he has done in the past. The only thing bad that happens to him is that he loses all influence over Carla's decisions, especially after how she bravely stood up to him.

characters.name: Beatriz Caleruega
characters.description: Abusive Parents: The first time she's introduced, she was an aloof neutral no-nonsense woman. However, in season 3, she's shown to be an absolute nightmare as a mother, although to a lesser extent. But that doesn't make her any better than Teo. When Carla tells her about her father forcing her to date Yeray (to whom she's not romantically interested and is clear she misses Samuel even if she won't admit it), as his wealth is their only hope for the wineries to not face bankruptcy, she stays quiet and Carla deduces that she was totally on board with her husband's plan, not even giving a damn about her daughter's needs and encouraging her to keep dating him. It's All About Me: She sides with her husband's plan to force Carla to date Yeray at any cost, so she wouldn't lose her wealthy lifestyle. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: In Season 3, only after she is revealed to have agreed with her husband's plan to set Carla up with Yeray in order to save the wineries from bankruptcy.The way she called her daughter out ("think about our future") was just too cruel. Karma Houdini: Ultimately, Beatriz gets no comeuppance for her part in prostituing her own daughter. Put on a Bus: She's not seen again after admitting to supporting Teo's plan with the wineries.

characters.name: Begoña and Andrea
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Polo's mothers are not physically abusive by any means, but they frequently belittle him and question his manhood on more than one occasion. Ascended Extra: They get more prominence in season 3, but mostly Begoña, who actively tries to stop Samuel and Guzman from bullying her son. The Bad Guy Wins: Only when they have Samuel and Guzman expelled the day they were supposed to graduate and cancelling Lu and Nadia's scholarships when they publicly bring up the accusations against him, but Polo feels guilty and realizes they've gone too far, so he admits to them that he actually killed Marina. While the damage with Samuel and Guzman is already done and knows he can't do anything to fix it, he does beg them to reinstate the scholarships.They do. Big Bad Ensemble: With Teo in season 3, about Polo's crime - but their agendas against the characters involved are different. Defrosting Ice Queen: Begoña, at the end of season 3after her son dies.

characters.name: Ventura Nunier
characters.description: Corrupt Corporate Executive: His company took shortcuts and used poor material when rebuilding Samuel, Nadia and Christian's old school which led to the building falling in and set the series in motion. The Bus Came Back: Makes two quick appearances with Laura in Season 3, first when they talk about Marina with Guzmán and later come to the school to protest their son's expulsion. Jerkass Has a Point: Despite his coldness to Marina, him and his wife has a right to be horrified and furious to his daughter when she helped Nano stole the watches from Carla’s dad. Though he reminds Marina that she is a minor and he even convinced her to end the pregnancy, which Marina refuses to.

characters.name: Armando de la Ossa
characters.description: Asshole Victim: In the fourth season finale, Armando is killed by Guzmán with a firework gun in retribution for sexually abusing Mencía and trying to kill Ari, so it's very hard to feel sorry for him. Rebeka even lampshaded it to Omar when he confronted her and Samuel for covering up the murder. Big Bad: In Season 4 for Mencia, entering a sexual relationship with her and threatening to use this against her family. Blackmail:He scares Mencía into staying with him by threatening to tell her family about her sex worker money-making scheme.In a flashback of season 5, it was revealed that Armando had blackmailed Benjamín with incrimating evidence that could ruin him unless he shared his part of the fortune. He scares Mencía into staying with him by threatening to tell her family about her sex worker money-making scheme. In a flashback of season 5, it was revealed that Armando had blackmailed Benjamín with incrimating evidence that could ruin him unless he shared his part of the fortune.

characters.name: Cruz Carvalho
characters.description: Asshole Victim: An unusualIn-Universeexample. Cruz was never a bad person at all, but as Iván points out his detractors think he deserved to die for being gay. Bury Your Gays: He gets brutally beaten to death by three homophobic men in season 6 after he publicly comes out as gay. Coming-Out Story: In early season 6, He announced to everyone that he is gay. Hypocrite: He gets upset at his son for having crushes on both Patrick and Ari, while he’s fooling around with Patrick and didn’t completely deny his sexuality. Nice Guy: Despite his immature ways, he seems to be very moral for Patrick and Ivan.

characters.name: Roberta
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Roberta is shown to be condescendingly neglectful to Isadora, not caring about the fact that she was raped by three guys. In season 8, she even goes a far to disown Isadora for her husband’s death after Isadora refusing to sell the club. Alas, Poor Villain: It's not too hard to at least feel a little sorry for Roberta, who was genuinely devastated to learn her husband was murdered in prison. Not that blaming and disowning Isadora justifies it. Absurdly Youthful Mother:Downplayed. Judging by the looks of it, Roberta is Isadora’s mother and her actress, Luz Cipriota was 37 on her first appearance. Asshole Victim: A non-fatal example. She's devastated when Martín is killed in season 8, but other than that, Roberta was generally an awful person, from repeatedly neglecting her daughter Isadora to even orchestrating a shooting at the school with a bunch of innocent underage students, and pinning the blame on Dídac's family to attempt to have him expelled. Blaming the Victim: As the person who's supposed to love her the most, this woman has the audacity to blame her own daughter for bringing the traumatic rape on herself, especially because she was drinking a lot and the clothes she wore were too revealing, which leaves Isadora heartbroken.

characters.name: Martín
characters.description: Affably Evil: He is a well-mannered gentleman despite his intimidating personality. Asshole Victim: For all of his crimes, including his attempted murder on Rocío and her mother, Martín won't be missed at all. Back for the Dead: Martín makes a small return in season 8, when Isadora visits him in prison and asks her to sell the club, so she can use the money to bail him out. However, he is killed by the inmates before the procedure could be done. Big Bad: He is one of the main villains in season 7. Becomes aBig Bad Ensemblewith Raúl. Blatant Lies: Martín threatens Dídac to stay away from Isadora. When Pau arrives and asks what's going on, Martín covers it up as a "friendly conversation".

characters.name: Carmen
characters.description: The Beard: She turned out to be this for Cruz as a way to silence the rumours about his sexuality. Gold Digger: She was initially after the money Iván inherited from his father. Hypocrite: Carmen stops Chloe from having sex with Ivan by informing he's her brother. However, despite being aware he's her son, she almost does the same to Ivan under the influence of the drugs. Mama Bear: She fiercely protects her daughter from Raul when he is violent to her, pushing him off the roof to his demise, and later giving a false alibi to the police. Parental Incest: She almost has an intimate yet gross moment with Iván when they are both on drugs. Carmen immediately realizes what she's doing and flees from his house disgusted and freaked out.

characters.name: Catalina
characters.description: Blatant Lies: Always lies to her own daughter Rocío about her involvement with Martin, which frustrates her and further strains their already distant relationship. Of course, Rocío won't take any of her mom's bullshit. Broken Pedestal: Rocío was implied to look up to her mother as a shining example of seeking justice, only to be disappointed after finding out about her corruption. Corrupt Bureaucrat: She's revealed to be corrupt as she's taking bribes from Isadora's father to push forward the eviction of a building owned by Isadora's House. Yet, everytime she says she won't be doing more favors because of her high position as a judge, Martin makes it clear he's the one who decides when he does or doesn't need her. He Knows Too Much: When Isadora teams up with the police to have her father arrested and arranges a meeting with Catalina at a restaurant to give her back some documents incriminating her in baby trafficking, however, he decides that she's of no more use to him and hires some thugs to kill Catalina as a way to keep her quiet. Hypocrite: Catalina is angry at Rocío for joining the social centre protest where she got arrested as she taught her a lot about justice, yet this woman has the gall to get involved in shady illegal business with Isadora's father and keeps lying to her poor daughter's face.

characters.name: Inspectora
characters.description: Flat Character: She doesn't get a lot of characterization other than interrogating the potential suspects involved. Put on a Bus: After the third season, she no longer appears and is replaced.

characters.name: Sebastián Abaga
characters.description: Put on a Bus: He doesn't appear again after season 5. Reasonable Authority Figure: The lieutenant correctly deduces that Samuel couldn't have killed Armando, and offers him a deal to expose Benjamín's illegal business in trafficking data of powerful people. Token Minority: One of the few black characters in the 4th and 5th season.

characters.name: Luis
characters.description: Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Luis immediately acts like a complete coward once he gets caught for Joel's murder and attempting to rape Isadora. Asshole Victim: No one absolutely cared that Isadora killed him for murdering Joel and attempting to get away with it. Bad Guys Do the Dirty Work: Arrests the powerful and wealthy Krawietz siblings without a question in support of Omar testifying against them for assaulting him. Beneath Suspicion: Because Luis is a cop, he is hardly found suspicious as Joel's killer, to the point that Eric and Chloe, the Krawietz siblings and Carmen are accused of killing him. Big Bad Ensemble: One of the main antagonists of season 8, along with Emilia and Héctor.

characters.name: Luena
characters.description: Et Tu, Brute?: Luena has this reaction upon finding out that Luis murdered Joel and is horrified for what he was about to do to Isadora. Everyone Has Standards: Luena might have wrongfully arrested Ivan and Dalmar for the murder of Joel, but she was completely apalled that Luis would be capable of attempting to rape Isadora that she quickly went in to arrest him. Same for what he did to Joel. Good Cop/Bad Cop: The good cop to Luis' bad cop, when Omar tries to denounce Joel's murder. Fiery Redhead: She doesn't hesitate to arrest her own partner Luis for Joel's murder and his attempt to rape and kill Isadora.
